messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@helixrx.com>, procurement@helixrx.com
Date: 2026-11-25T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Request: temporary surcharge cap and proactive reserve lien for HelixRx (HLX-3847)

Team —

Quick summary: HelixRx (HLX-3847) is asking for a temporary concession to move forward this quarter. They want two non-standard items: a temporary surcharge cap on burst overage rates and a reservation hold (we call this a proactive reserve lien) to protect their ability to burst to H100-equivalent capacity while we finalize Dedicated provisioning. They are offering a higher committed spend in exchange and want a short window to validate performance.

Ask: Can Deal Desk / Exec approve the temporary concession described below? I need a clear yes/no and any guardrails we want (time limit, ramp, reconciliation).

What HelixRx requested:
- Reservation hold: 6 H100-equivalent GPUs for up to 3 weeks (to be prioritized in the US-west pool)
- Temporary overage surcharge cap: $0.45/hr per GPU-equivalent for any burst usage during the hold window (cap applies to the first 3 weeks)
- Commitment: they will convert to a 3-month reserved commitment if concession granted; proposed committed spend $125,000 minimum

Why this matters:
- We can secure a mid-market customer that will likely expand to Dedicated; the window aligns with their internal launch and churn risk is non-trivial if they can't guarantee burst capacity.
- Short-term margin hit if we cap surcharge; offset by committed revenue and potential 12–18% longer-term renewal.

Attached: helix_term_sheet_v3.pdf and their Q4 usage forecast (usage_forecast_Q4.csv).

Risks/notes:
- We will need Legal to add a clause for "reservation lien" that allows us to prioritize their burst but also to bill actuals if they exceed agreed thresholds after the hold window.
- Finance: this reduces overage rate upside for up to three weeks. We should pick a reconciliation mechanism post-hold (true-up or credit).

Proposed guardrail (my recommendation): Approve the reservation hold and surcharge cap for a 21-day window only, with a mandatory reconciliation: if actual burst costs exceed projected by >20%, we split the delta 50/50 and schedule immediate remediation. Also require DocuSign signature and procurement acceptance by EOD next Tuesday.

Next step: Karthik / Lauren — can you review margin exposure and legal language. Marissa — can you run capacity planning to confirm the US-west pool can absorb a 6 H100-equivalent hold for those dates?

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: helix_term_sheet_v3.pdf, usage_forecast_Q4.csv

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T11:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary surcharge cap and proactive reserve lien for HelixRx (HLX-3847)

Naomi — thanks for the clear ask and the docs. I ran a quick margin calc with Finance. A few notes: 

1) Margin impact: capping at $0.45/hr will reduce short-term overage revenue by ~38% relative to our standard burst surcharge for H100-equivalents (based on forecasted utilization). That is material but manageable if we get the committed $125k.

2) Alternative I recommend: Approve a stepped cap to reduce risk: $0.60/hr for week 1, $0.45/hr for week 2, and $0.45/hr with an optional extension only if they sign the 3-month reserved commitment within the window. This gives us downside protection while demonstrating flexibility.

3) Reconciliation: Strongly prefer a post-window true-up (actual cost vs. billed cap). If HelixRx agrees, we can bill the capped amount up-front and then invoice any delta after reconciliation. That protects cash flow.

4) Legal/operational: We must ensure the SLA for prioritized allocation doesn't violate fairness to other customers; recommend we limit the reservation lien to a named pool and allow auto-preempt if actual cluster pressure exceeds 90% for >1 hour.

If leadership signs off on the stepped cap, I'm comfortable escalating for an Exec concession.

-Karthik
Head of Deal Desk
Redwood Inference

- We can increase the commitment to $150k for the quarter if Redwood can confirm the stepped cap Karthik proposed (we prefer predictability and the week-1 higher cap is acceptable).
- Procurement is preparing a DocuSign packet — we need the legal language for the reservation lien and the timebound cap added to the term sheet. I can get signatures within 48 hours once terms are final.

Naomi / Karthik — I spoke with Legal and Finance this morning. High level: I'm prepared to approve the stepped surcharge cap and the reservation hold on the conditions below. This counts as an Exec-level concession so I'm marking it urgent.

Conditions for approval (must be in the term sheet):
- Stepped cap as Karthik suggested: $0.60/hr (week 1) -> $0.45/hr (week 2+), with an automatic expiration at 21 days unless they sign the reserved 3-month commitment for $150k.
- Reservation lien: explicit window dates and us-west pool only; clause allowing us to reclaim the hold if cluster pressure exceeds 90% for >1 hour.
- Reconciliation: 7-day true-up with itemized usage report; any delta >20% to be split 50/50.
- Discount: Approve an additional 2% one-time concession (on top of standard pricing) conditional on DocuSign signature within 48 hours of the final term sheet.

Operational ask to Marissa: please confirm capacity on US-west for dates Dec 1–Dec 21 and note any maintenance windows or known preemptions. If capacity checks out, Legal will insert the lien language and Procurement can execute the DocuSign packet.

I'll call out to Exec if anything changes, but you have my conditional sign-off.

Lauren Bishop
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
